0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Vouvray lies in the heart of Touraine, spanning 8 villages and about 2,000–3,000 hectares of vineyards (sources vary), and is one of the few regions in the world that can produce everything from bone-dry wines to botrytised sweet wines to traditional-method sparkling wines within a single AOC. Its diversity comes from one variety — Chenin Blanc — and from tuffeau, a parent rock that can "breathe."

Learning Objectives

📐 The four-level sweetness system

Under EU labelling rules, fully grasp the residual-sugar standards and tasting features of Sec / Demi-Sec / Moelleux / Doux (Liquoreux)

🪨 Tuffeau terroir

Understand how this porous, chalky parent rock gives Chenin Blanc mineral depth and ageing potential

🍇 Three sweet-wine production methods

Distinguish noble rot (Botrytis), raisining on the vine (Passerillage) and late harvest (Tries)

🥂 Vouvray Mousseux/Pétillant

Get to know Vouvray's traditional-method sparkling line — sparkling wine makes up a significant share of Vouvray's output

1.content:
Vouvray lies east of the city of Tours, on the north bank of the Loire. The AOC covers 8 villages: Vouvray, Vernou-sur-Brenne, Sainte-Radegonde, Rochecorbon, Chançay, Noizay, Reugny and Parçay-Meslay. Most vineyards are planted on tuffeau parent rock on the high slopes above the river, and beneath them lie many cellar tunnels left from the 19th century (Cave Troglodyte).

📐 Vouvray basic data

  • Area: about 2,000–3,000 hectares (sources vary)
  • Variety: 100% Chenin Blanc
  • Soils: tuffeau, Aubuis (clay-limestone), Perruches (clay-flint)
  • Climate: mild continental, moderated by the Loire
  • Annual output: about 120,000 hL, of which about 60% is sparkling
  • Sparkling labelling: Vouvray Mousseux (traditional method), Vouvray Pétillant (semi-sparkling, pressure about 1–2.5 atm)
1.quiz.question: What variety does the Vouvray AOC require?
1.quiz.explanation: Vouvray is a single-variety Chenin Blanc AOC, and blending other varieties is forbidden. This rule ensures every Vouvray is a pure reflection of Chenin's response to terroir and vintage conditions; the different sweetness levels and sparkling styles come entirely from winemaking choices and vintage conditions.

4.title: Tuffeau — The Parent Rock That Breathes
4.highlights.0.title: Porous and hygroscopic
4.highlights.0.content: Porosity as high as 45%, able to absorb and release moisture, regulating water in the root zone
4.highlights.1.title: Castle building stone
4.highlights.1.content: The snow-white walls of the Loire châteaux (Chambord, Chenonceau and others) are cut from tuffeau blocks
4.highlights.2.title: Underground cellars
4.highlights.2.content: Tunnels left after 19th-century quarrying became natural cellars, at 12°C and 85% humidity all year
4.content:
Tuffeau is the key terroir shared by middle-Loire regions such as Vouvray, Montlouis, Saumur and Chinon. It formed from shallow-sea sediments of the late Cretaceous (Turonian, about 90 million years ago), cemented mainly from foraminifera, sponge spicules and quartz sand, with a soft, snow-white, porous texture.

🌊 Formation and structure

  • Cretaceous shallow-sea sediment, rich in calcium carbonate at 50–60%
  • Porosity as high as 45%, soft and easy to cut
  • Divided into Tuffeau Blanc (white) and Tuffeau Jaune (yellow, containing glassy sponge spicules)

🌱 Effect on the vines

  • Water regulation: the porous structure retains water without waterlogging, letting vine roots draw water steadily in drought years
  • Mineral supply: rich in calcium carbonate, giving Chenin its chalky mineral tension
  • Temperature moderation: the white colour reflects sunlight, easing high temperatures during ripening

🍷 Effect on flavour

  • Chalky mineral texture, wet stone, beeswax, chamomile
  • High-acid structure (pH usually 3.0–3.2)
  • 10+ years of ageing potential, developing candied apple, roasted hazelnut and foie-gras flavours
4.quiz.question: Tuffeau's porosity is as high as 45% — what is the main effect of this on viticulture?
4.quiz.options.0: Vine roots struggle to take hold
4.quiz.options.1: It absorbs and releases water, supplying the vines steadily in drought years
4.quiz.explanation: Tuffeau's high porosity (45%) makes it like a natural sponge — absorbing water when it rains and releasing it slowly to the root zone in drought. This is especially critical in extreme drought years such as 2003, 2018 and 2022, letting Vouvray's Chenin Blanc keep balanced acidity and ripeness even in dry years. The same property also makes tuffeau an ideal cellar material.

6.title: Vouvray Sparkling — France's Forgotten Sparkling Speciality
6.highlights.0.title: Traditional method
6.highlights.0.content: Vouvray Mousseux follows the same rules as the Méthode Champenoise (second fermentation in the bottle)
6.highlights.1.title: Two pressure levels
6.highlights.1.content: Mousseux (fully sparkling, ≥ 3.5 atm) and Pétillant (semi-sparkling, about 1–2.5 atm) coexist
6.highlights.2.title: Remarkable output
6.highlights.2.content: 60% of Vouvray's output is sparkling, making it one of France's important bottle-fermented regions
6.content:
Many people don't know that Vouvray's sparkling output is much larger than its still wine — a tradition going back to the late 19th century, when Chenin Blanc's high acidity, combined with the convenience of rail transport, made Vouvray an affordable stand-in for Champagne on Paris dining tables. Today's Vouvray Mousseux/Pétillant continues this tradition and is the highest model of Chenin Blanc sparkling wine.

🥂 Vouvray Mousseux (≥ 3.5 atm)

  • Second fermentation in the bottle (Méthode Traditionnelle)
  • Minimum ageing of 12 months (12–24 months at most estates)
  • Style: green apple, white flowers, toast, chalky minerality
  • Commonly: Brut (≤ 12 g/L residual sugar), Sec, Demi-Sec

🫧 Vouvray Pétillant (about 1–2.5 atm)

  • Semi-sparkling style (closer to Frizzante)
  • Fine bubbles, a softer mouthfeel
  • A traditional table-wine choice, paired with pork charcuterie and cream-sauce dishes

🌟 Representative producers

  • Domaine Huet (King of Vouvray): the Pétillant range is especially classic, and Le Mont Pétillant can be cellared 20+ years
  • François Pinon: organic, natural-wine style, with an extremely pure Brut Non Dosé
  • Vincent Carême: a new-generation figure, returning to the ancestral method with Ancestrale (Pét-Nat)
  • Domaine de la Taille aux Loups: Jacky Blot's estate, spanning Vouvray + Montlouis
7.title: Level 3-6 Knowledge Check
7.questions.0.question: What is the residual-sugar range for Demi-Sec in the Vouvray AOC?
7.questions.0.explanation: Under EU labelling rules, the sweetness levels are: Sec (≤ 4 g/L, up to 9 when balanced by acidity), Demi-Sec (4–12 g/L, up to 18), Moelleux (12–45 g/L), Doux/Liquoreux (> 45 g/L, often botrytised). Demi-Sec is Vouvray's most representative style, often seen as the most natural expression of Chenin Blanc and tuffeau terroir.
7.questions.1.question: Roughly what proportion of Vouvray's output is sparkling?
7.questions.1.explanation: About 60% of Vouvray's output is sparkling (Mousseux + Pétillant), making it one of France's important bottle-fermented regions. The tradition goes back to the late 19th century, when the railway carried Vouvray's high-acid Chenin to Paris as an affordable stand-in for Champagne.
7.questions.2.question: How does Vouvray's sweet wine mainly accumulate sugar? (Choose the most common)
7.questions.2.explanation: Vouvray's Moelleux and Liquoreux rely mainly on Botrytis cinerea (noble rot) infection. The Loire and Brenne valleys produce morning mist in autumn (triggering noble rot) and dry afternoon sun (preventing grey rot), ideal conditions for noble rot to develop. Passerillage (raisining on the vine) and successive picking (Tries) are also used. The AOC forbids added sugar (chaptalisation does not apply to sweet-wine levels).
7.questions.3.question: When did Tuffeau form, and what is it mainly composed of?
7.questions.3.options.0: Late Jurassic, containing Exogyra oyster fossils
7.questions.3.options.1: Late Cretaceous, containing calcium carbonate and sponge spicules
7.questions.3.explanation: Tuffeau formed in the late Cretaceous (Turonian, about 90 million years ago), and is composed mainly of calcium carbonate (50–60%), glassy sponge spicules and quartz sand. It is entirely different from the late Jurassic Kimmeridgian (the soil of Sancerre/Chablis), which explains why the Chenin/Sauvignon styles of the middle Loire and the central Loire are so clearly different.
